title: Chapter 36: Danger
html:
After several seconds, Brother Feng managed to point toward the washroom. “The mirror…”

That single word changed Chen Ge’s expression. He made sure Brother Feng was settled, then looked inside. The wall mirror had shattered, scattering pieces across the floor.

After He San’s earlier incident, Chen Ge had covered every mirror he knew about with black cloth. No further problems had occurred. With the new scenario, however, he had failed to repeat the precaution everywhere—and now a visitor had been frightened badly enough to break one.

For an entertainment business, a reputation for unsafe conditions could be disastrous. Chen Ge stared at the broken mirror from the doorway. “I need to solve this problem before anyone else gets hurt.”

Whatever the thing in the mirrors was, Chen Ge no longer regarded it as a harmless curiosity. Both He San and Brother Feng had encountered it, and the pattern was becoming impossible to dismiss.

Covering mirrors was only a temporary measure. As long as the phenomenon remained unexplained, the new scenario could not safely stay open. Finding nothing else unusual in the washroom, Chen Ge returned to Brother Feng.

He sat beside him. “Can you tell me what happened?”

After a few minutes, Brother Feng’s breathing steadied, although his face remained pale. “I’m not sure I can explain it properly.”

“That’s fine. Just tell me what you remember.” Chen Ge listened carefully. Unlike He San, Brother Feng had remained conscious throughout the experience, which meant he might be able to describe far more.

“One of your actors was chasing us, so I hid in this room. At first everything was normal. Then I started feeling as if someone were calling me.”

“Calling your name?”

“Not exactly. More like… pulling my attention somewhere.” Brother Feng frowned. “It took me a while to realize the feeling was coming from inside this room.”

His expression tightened. “From the mirror in the washroom. I thought I could hear something through it, but I couldn’t make out words. I only knew it felt directed at me.”

“What happened next?” Chen Ge committed every detail to memory.

“I stood in front of the mirror because I wanted to understand it. The closer I got, the less normal I felt. My reflection started to seem slightly out of sync—not obviously wrong, but wrong enough that I knew something had changed.” He glanced uneasily toward the washroom. “The strangest part was that I wasn’t frightened at first. That’s what scares me now.”

“What do you mean?”

Brother Feng took a slow breath. “I leaned closer, and the face in the mirror leaned closer too. It looked exactly like me, but I had this certainty that it wasn’t me. Then I realized my body was moving before I consciously decided to move. For a moment it felt as though I couldn’t tell which side of the glass I was standing on.”

That description was disturbingly close to what Chen Ge had experienced during his own Nightmare Mission. “What snapped you out of it?”

“Oddly enough, the mirror did.” Brother Feng gave a humorless laugh at Chen Ge’s confusion. “I saw a rag doll behind me in the reflection.”

“A rag doll?”

“One of the small ones scattered through the set. About this big, with a stitched beard.” Brother Feng held his hands apart. “Seeing it suddenly scared me enough to realize something was wrong. My mind wanted to get away even though my body was slow to respond.”

Brother Feng spoke calmly now, but Chen Ge could imagine how frightening the moment must have been.

“Then I heard He San shouting from somewhere downstairs. That broke whatever hold the mirror had on me. I panicked and knocked the mirror down with the chair. I know this is a park attraction, but in that moment I completely forgot.”

Brother Feng looked embarrassed. “Everything I’ve told you is true. I’ll pay for the damaged mirror.”

“Forget the mirror. I’m just glad you’re okay.” Chen Ge looked around the room. “Where is the doll you saw?”

Brother Feng hesitated. “I think it ended up under the bed. That’s one of your props, isn’t it? Sorry.”

Chen Ge crouched and retrieved the bearded doll from beneath the bed. A dusty shoe mark crossed its fabric. He brushed it clean. “You may owe this little guy a thank-you.”

“The doll saved me?” Brother Feng edged backward. “If you say so. Thank you, doll. Can I leave now?”

“One question first. If I told you what happened wasn’t part of the attraction at all, would you believe me?”

Still wearing most of the Doctor Skull-Cracker costume and holding the battered doll, Chen Ge probably could not have chosen a less reassuring moment to ask.

Brother Feng, who was nearly 190 centimeters tall, pressed farther into the corner of the bed. “I genuinely don’t know what answer you want from me.”
